title: 未縮寫 negative questions with not 的強調用法
sentences: Do we not owe the volunteers some recompense for three weekends of work?
Is the argument not tangential to everything we came here to decide?
Does the report not strike you as nebulous on the one point that matters?
Are we not adamant that the deadline will hold?
Did the committee not promise a decision before the recess?
Is it not germane to ask who paid for the study?
Can we not obviate the whole quandary by asking the tenants first?
Should the board not have foreseen a shortfall this obvious?
Have we not heard this same impromptu excuse twice already?
Was the second witness not the more circumspect of the two?
Would it not be frugal to repair the old printing press instead of buying a new one?
Do the figures not look pernicious once you separate out the subsidy?
Are they not aware that the soil here is arid for most of the year?
Is a single tedious meeting not a small price for getting this settled?
Has the minister not been stubborn about this from the first day?
Could we not construe her silence as consent?
Do you not find it grievous that no one was told?
Is the young architect not the most iconoclastic hire we have made?
Will the delay not antagonize the very people we need on our side?
Did you not promise to waive the fee for first-time applicants?
Are these claims not worth corroborating before we print them?
Is it not shameless to ask for a raise in the same week the layoffs were announced?
Does a pithy summary not serve the reader better than four pages?
Have the tenants not shown remarkable modesty about what they are owed?
Is the new logo not a little too flamboyant for a law firm?
Can the museum not open one solitary room while the rest is repaired?
Do we not owe the reader a plainer word than this jargon?
Was his apology not a little too impassive to be believed?
Should we not relent now that both families have apologized?
Is the evidence not relevant simply because it arrived late?
Does the contract not oblige them to cover the reimbursement?
Are we not all fallible on a night with this little sleep?
Is the applicant's probity not the one thing we cannot test on paper?
Do they not see that a nascent programme needs two years, not two months?
Is the current government not responsible for the state of the railways?
canDo: Can form negative questions with uncontracted 'not' to emphasise a point in an argument.

title: would hate to：把很不希望說得客氣而堅定
sentences: I'd hate to intrude on what looks like a rare moment of serenity.
She would hate to come across as supercilious in front of the new team.
We would hate to see a project this promising sink into a quagmire of approvals.
He'd hate to be thought maladroit at his own farewell party.
I would hate to reprimand you twice for the same oversight.
They would hate to lose a client whose probity has never once been in question.
Our supervisor would hate to sound churlish, but the deadline has not moved.
I'd hate to intensify a disagreement that both sides have almost forgotten.
She would hate to be remembered for one perfunctory performance.
The auditor would hate to discover that the whole department is a sham.
I would hate to seem obsequious, so I will say plainly that the plan is weak.
He would hate to spend his senescence in a house this cold.
We would hate to improvise in front of an audience that has paid this much.
My mother would hate to arrive anywhere looking less than presentable.
I'd hate to give you a flat refusal, but the budget simply is not there.
The committee would hate to relent now, after two years of holding the line.
She would hate to be the one who has to specify what went wrong.
He would hate to lose his composure in front of the whole board.
We'd hate to leave the new hire with a dearth of examples to work from.
She would hate to be described as intransigent when she has already conceded twice.
They would hate to rebuff an offer made in such good faith.
The old man would hate to admit that his memory now depends on mnemonics.
I would hate to answer with the sort of equivocation you get from a spokesman.
She would hate to appear miserly at a party she suggested herself.
I'd hate to see a gregarious child pushed into a job this solitary.
He would hate to be caught out by a question from a tyro.
The doctor would hate to alarm you, but that sallow colour is worth a test.
I would hate to work under a hidebound manager after three years of freedom.
She would hate to let a single woeful review undo a year of steady work.
I'd hate not to say this while I still have the nerve: the schedule is impossible.
She would hate it if her brisk manner were taken for indifference.
They would hate it if a blatant leak forced the announcement forward a week.
I would hate it if my silence were read as assent.
I'd hate not to give the report a proper critique just because time is short.
She would hate not to be there when her guileless younger brother signs the lease.
canDo: Can use 'would hate' + 'to' infinitive, for emphasis.

title: 含有直接受詞的片語介系詞動詞

If the invitation is still open, I'd like to take you up on it.

I put the mistake down to tiredness rather than carelessness.

Don't take your bad mood out on the children.
Could you put me through to whoever handles refunds?
My aunt keeps trying to fix me up with her neighbour's son.
The magistrate let her off with a fine and a warning.
I missed your birthday, and I intend to make it up to you.
He played the two suppliers off against each other until the price came down.
They tried to pass a nineteenth-century copy off as a sixteenth-century original.
The committee wrote the entire episode off as a misunderstanding.
My editor pulled me up on the same comma three times in one afternoon.
Mum signed us up for swimming lessons without asking either of us.
I had no idea what that one small favour was letting me in for.
It took two long meetings to bring the board round to the idea.
She handed the whole file over to the police the following morning.
They put the flat up for sale a week after the wedding.
I put him down as the quiet type the moment he walked in, and I was wrong.
Bring it up with her directly instead of going through me.
Good luck pinning him down to an actual date.
The contract ties you down to three years, so read it twice before you sign.
They set a small room aside for anyone who needed to step out for a while.
He held the worst of the diagnosis back from his parents for the best part of a month.
If you want to use my contacts, cut me in on whatever you make.
They shut her out of every decision that actually mattered.
Leave me out of whatever you two are arguing about this time.

Give her a week and she will talk you round to her way of seeing it.

The smell of the corridor took her back to her grandmother's kitchen.
guideword: FORM: VERB + DIRECT OBJECT + PARTICLE + PREPOSITION + OBJECT
canDo: Can use a direct object with some prepositional verbs as well as an object of the preposition.
